Monthly rate $r=\dfrac{0.059}{12}=0.00491667$

Payment: $\text{PMT}=P\dfrac{r}{1-(1+r)^{-n}}$, $P=35000$
Total cost $=\text{PMT}\times n-P+\text{fee}$

**Loan A:** $n=72$, fee $=0$
$(1+r)^{72}\approx1.42352$
$\text{PMT}=35000\frac{0.00491667}{1-1.42352^{-1}}\approx \$578.40$
Total $=578.40\times72-35000\approx \$6,644.82$

**Loan B:** $n=60$, fee $=0$
$(1+r)^{60}\approx1.34216$
$\text{PMT}\approx \$675.02$
Total $=675.02\times60-35000\approx \$5,501.31$

**Loan C:** $n=36$, fee $=0.02\times35000=\$700$
$(1+r)^{36}\approx1.19311$
$\text{PMT}\approx \$1,063.18$
Interest $=1063.18\times36-35000\approx \$3,274.58$
Total $=3,274.58+700\approx \$3,974.58$

Loan C is cheapest, despite the fee.
